title: Diagnostics, Calibration, Test & Acceptance Runtime
objective: Implement engineering-specific inspection evidence, fault isolation, calibration/tuning/alignment, bounded test/shakedown/acceptance evidence, and MERA interpretation of PCA-12/Packet-08 analyses without creating a generic solver, hidden-truth oracle, or owner-state mutation path.
acceptance: Observed symptom evidence remains distinct from suspected, isolated and identified fault state.
Unavailable evidence cannot reveal hidden fault truth through diagnostics or errors.
Calibration/tuning changes only governed adjustable state and cannot invent unsupported capability.
PCA-12/Packet-08 solver or simulation output remains noncanonical evidence about a declared model.
UNKNOWN, timeout and unsupported analysis dimensions remain inconclusive rather than pass/fail.
Successful repair evidence does not itself prove acceptance; required acceptance testing remains separately governed.
Failed acceptance preserves prior successful owner receipts/history.
Owner-defined certification requirements are enforced without inventing universal real-world engineering standards.
Blocking diagnostics/test flows remain semantic/nonvisual and provider-off.
boundaries: MERA-01 and MERA-03 remain sealed predecessors.
D17/PPIA-03 retain live Asset state; MIB-12 retains repair transaction authority.
MRCS retains reusable engineering/fault/test/calibration definition authority.
MERA-06+ disassembly, repair, network/failure and domain adapter work remains unauthorized.
MBES-01 rotation milestone is satisfied but MBES start remains blocked until the MERA program completes because ROADMAP_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH hard_requires MERA and MBES backlog activation_after MERA-24.
